title: Super-chunky lap throw
subtitle: A bold 100 by 120 cm lap throw in super-chunky wool on 10 mm needles.
excerpt: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw worked flat in garter stitch on 10 mm needles using approximately 900 g of super-chunky wool. Super-chunky yarn at 10 mm produces a dramatically fast knit: the throw casts on 50 stitches and each garter row takes minutes.
sourceNotes: Super-chunky-weight throws are a contemporary application of the single-panel garter construction documented in Weldon's Practical Knitter (1880s). Craft Yarn Council CYC 6 super-chunky standards place the weight class at 7 to 11 stitches per 10 cm on 9 to 15 mm needles.

knitting.gaugeText: 10 sts × 20 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 10 mm needles, unblocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A yarn weight class rated CYC 6 by the Craft Yarn Council, knitting to approximately 7 to 11 stitches per 10 cm on 9 to 15 mm needles. Also called super-bulky in US terminology. Produces very warm, dramatic fabric that knits quickly.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat in garter stitch on 10 mm needles in
super-chunky wool
, finishing at 100 cm wide by 120 cm long.

A single panel requires no seaming and the wide needle size makes the most of super-chunky yarn's speed advantage. Super-chunky was chosen to produce a throw that is noticeably faster than any DK or aran blanket in this collection; at 10 mm the cast-on is only 100 stitches and a garter row passes in a minute or two. Budget about 900 g (about 360 m / 395 yards) of super-chunky wool or super-chunky wool blend. Super-chunky skeins are typically 100 to 200 g each; buy eight to ten skeins in matched dye lots. A dye-lot shift in super-chunky yarn reads at high contrast because of the yarn's bulk. Drapes over a sofa end or lays across the lap; too heavy and bulky to fold compact for a bag.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 900 g (about 360 m / 395 yards) of super-chunky-weight wool or wool blend
items.substitutions: CYC 6 British wool, super-chunky merino, or a wool-acrylic blend at CYC 6. Avoid pure acrylic super-chunky that will steam-block permanently and lose its loft.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 10 mm (UK 000 / US 15) circular needle, 100 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

10 stitches and 20 rows to 10 cm over garter stitch on 10 mm needles, unblocked. Super-chunky yarn varies considerably between brands; a CYC 6 yarn can run from 7 to 12 stitches per 10 cm. Swatch with the actual yarn before casting on the throw. If your gauge is 9 stitches per 10 cm with a 100-stitch cast-on, the throw will be about 111 cm wide rather than 100 cm. Adjust the cast-on count to an even number for your target width.
Row gauge matters less for a blanket worked to a measured length, but at 18 rows per 10 cm instead of 20, the throw will be about 13 cm shorter at 240 rows. Measure by tape.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast-on

Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 100 stitches. Long-tail tail: (10 × 100) / 10 + 15 = 100 + 15 = 115 cm. Measure 130 cm of tail; super-chunky yarn is thick enough that each stitch uses substantially more tail than DK.
Body

Knit every row until the throw measures 120 cm from the cast-on edge. At gauge that is 240 rows, but measuring by tape is more reliable. When you set this aside between sessions, the point in a garter throw is always obvious: all rows are knit rows, so you can pick up immediately without any tracking.
Stitch count check-ins
At row 120 (about 60 cm): count across the needle. You should have 100 stitches. At row 238 (about 119 cm): count again before the final cast-off row.
Common faults

Stitches splitting around the needle: super-chunky yarn with low twist can wrap around the needle tip rather than sitting cleanly on the shaft. Use smooth-tipped needles and check that each stitch is fully on the needle before working it.

Dropped stitch running quickly: at 10 mm needle size, dropped stitches run through five or six rows in seconds. Use locking stitch markers to secure the first and last stitch of any row where you suspect a stitch has dropped, and address runs before continuing.

Dye-lot shift visible mid-throw: particularly prominent in super-chunky because each row is wide and the yarn is fat. Buy all skeins in matched lots; if lots are unavoidable, alternate skeins every two rows.
Cast-off
Cast off knitwise with a very loose tension. Super-chunky cast-offs bind tightly; work each stitch with a deliberate looseness and pass the right needle through the stitch wider than feels natural.
Finishing
Thread a large-eyed tapestry needle with each tail and weave along a garter ridge for at least 5 cm, changing direction once. Trim. Super-chunky garter lies flat without blocking.
Care

Hand wash in cool water for non-superwash super-chunky wool. Machine wash only on the gentlest cycle at 30 degrees if the yarn label explicitly permits it. Lay flat to dry on a clean floor or table: a throw this size and weight cannot be hung without distorting. Allow a full day to dry.
What to try next

From a super-chunky garter throw, try a striped version next. Keep the same cast-on and construction. Alternate two colours every four rows. Carry both colours up the edge as in any striped garter project. The stripe effect is bolder at this scale.
